alex_k: quick heads-up from the 32k-seq regression run — a bunch of runs hit OOMs around 13–15k tokens even though we used the new small-block allocator knobs. attaching short trace and notes.

priya_m: ugh, saw that on my cluster too. any idea if it's allocator fragmentation or KV cache growth?

alex_k: initial profiler points to two things: (1) kernel selection fell back from fast fused-attn to the fallback path for long prefixes, which increases workspace temporarily, and (2) blockmgr compaction didn't trigger early because free-run threshold was too high, so we had a few big live holes. combined effect pushes GPU > reserved WS and OOM.

miguel_r: can you paste the perf counters you captured? even rough numbers help.

alex_k: pasted below — this is one failing trace from a 4-GPU dedicated worker with 2 workers per GPU. timestamps removed for brevity.

```
ATTN_KERNEL: fused_attn_fast -> fallback_slow
WORKSPACE_USAGE_MB: 824 -> spike 1350 -> evict attempt -> 1408 OOM
KV_CACHE_BYTES: 420MB -> peaks 1.1GB (per worker) during generation
BLOCK_FREE_FRAGMENTS: 12 -> 3 after attempted compaction (no success)
COMPACTION_RUNS: 1 (no merge, threshold not met)
BATCH_SIZE: 8 -> auto-batched to 12 by scheduler
```

sasha_l: interesting that batching increased to 12 — did the scheduler use cross-request batching policy with latency target off? that could blow up WS if requests have large prefixes.

leo_f: scheduler logs show we allowed latency SLO = 300ms and enabled aggressive batching. for long seq tests we should cap batching differently (e.g., max_effective_batch = 4 for >8k prefix).

priya_m: agreed. two concrete knobs to try: reduce max cross-batch size for long-seq profiles, and lower compaction threshold so blockmgr runs earlier. but compaction cost can regress latency — tradeoff.

miguel_r: also let's validate kernel selection rules: why is fused_attn_fast flipping to fallback_slow? maybe sequence length crossing a threshold triggers different kernel with higher WS. could be kernel heuristics using median-seqlen, not max.

alex_k: correct. kernel picker uses hist-based decision on seq distribution; when a single request with 32k arrives, median stays low so we still pick the "fast" kernel initially, but during generation we switch to fallback that needs bigger temporary buffers for streaming KV integration. switching moment triggers fragmentation because we allocated blocks for old pattern.

perf-ci-bot: regression alert: perf/long-seq/throughput decreased by 21% in canary 2026-03-15-rt1. Ticket: INF-2217. :rotating_light:

sasha_l: propose short experiment plan: (1) run long-seq with batching cap 4 and compaction threshold at 0.25 (currently 0.5) (2) enable eager block coalescing every N=50 allocations (cheap amortized check) (3) instrument kernel picker to prefer stable kernel when streaming KV will grow.

leo_f: add an option to pre-reserve extra WS slack when predicted streaming-kv growth > 512MB; if we reserve, we avoid mid-flight realloc and fragmentation. cheap safety margin may solve most OOMs.

priya_m: can we do a low-risk rollout? i) flip batching cap in canary only, ii) enable compaction threshold change behind feature flag, iii) add pre-reserve in dedicated-only build. then observe OOM count and median latency.

alex_k: sounds good. i'll bench the three combos today and push traces. quick notes on commands I used to reproduce:

```
# reproduce harness (docker run on dev-server)
./run_long_seq_test --model redwood-xxl --tokens 32000 --concurrency 6 --batching=auto --batch-cap=12 --log-trace
# compaction debug dump
rd-blockmgr dump --json | jq '.blocks | map({size, state, free_span})'
# kernel picker verbose
./runtime --kernel-debug=on --kernel-picker-hist 50
```

miguel_r: awesome. if we can get dumps from rd-blockmgr across the failing runs that'll help pinpoint whether compaction logic is miscalculating adjacent free spans.

perf-ci-bot: CI note: schedule job perf/long-seq/debug-dumps for canary on 2026-03-16T02:00Z.

sasha_l: action items: alex run experiments + upload three traces; leo add pre-reserve patch behind flag; priya coordinate canary config; miguel analyze block dump diff. please add results here. :thumbsup:

alex_k: I ran the first experiment (batch-cap=4, compaction threshold=0.25). preliminary results: no OOMs in 100 runs; median latency +6% but p95 unchanged. attaching condensed dump:

```
RESULT: 100/100 success, median lat 320ms -> 340ms, p95 560ms
BLOCK_FRAG_AFTER: avg fragments 4 (was 12)
KV_PEAK_PER_WORKER: 520MB
WORKSPACE_PEAK_MB: 820MB
```

miguel_r: promising. can we keep compaction threshold at 0.25 and test with eager coalesce patch? might bring latency back down.

leo_f: I'll open a small PR for pre-reserve flag today; default off. will link PR here once ready.

priya_m: great. marking this thread INF-2217/epic-blockmgr for tracking. please paste links to traces (s3 or buildkite) and I'll add to the regression dashboard.

alex_k: uploaded traces: s3://redwood-perf/longseq/1719991111/trace1.tar.gz and s3://redwood-perf/longseq/1719991111/blockdumps.json

sasha_l: leaving :eyes: — will follow up with latency/obs tradeoff analysis after eager coalesce run.

leo_f: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3139 (pre-reserve WS flag). comments welcome.

miguel_r: next steps for me: diff block dumps and produce a small script to classify fragment shapes (isolated vs adjacent). will post results tomorrow.

alex_k: thanks all — good progress. I'll keep canary running overnight and report back in morning.

perf-ci-bot: note: no new OOM regressions detected in canary with batch-cap=4 (12h window), summary uploaded.
